title: Level 1 (Beginner) - B-17
notes:
West leads the ♥10 against 6NT. South should win the opening heart lead and play on clubs. South can afford to lose 1 trick in clubs, but not 2. The only problem can occur when one defender has all 3 outstanding clubs.

There are two ways to play the club suit to guarantee only 1 loser, regardless of how that suit divides. First, South can start by leading a small club out of his hand. If West follows with the ♣5, a low club is played from dummy. If West discards on South's club lead, the ♣A is played from North. A club is led towards South's ♣Q, holding East to 1 club trick.

Alternatively, South can cross to dummy in spades and play a club towards his ♣Q. If East plays any club, South has an easy time. If East discards, South can play either a low club or the ♣Q and later finesse against West's other club honour.
